summary: legal checked in 3 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary: Risk disposition: blocked for SearchWoot public beta or full launch; conditional for ordinary reversible fleet growth; counsel_required for upstream data rights, jurisdiction-specific privacy treatment, vendor/DPA obligations, and future affiliate or advertising use. Exact decision: keep SearchWoot private. Evidence: official API documentation establishes access mechanics but not rights to store, transform, cache, display, alert on, or monetize returned data; current public terms point against the proposed use. Fleet compliance is technical baseline only: 37 pass, 16 fail, 6 unknown. Analytics and revenue attribution remain yellow; aggregate commission is unattributed and site-attributed commission is $0. Do not claim certification, ROI, or site-attributed revenue.

Launch-readiness tracking remains active: 0 of 4 legal tasks are closed. Partial evidence exists for official API documentation and terms, repository/configuration data-flow files, privacy and cookie pages, and draft terms; no task is closable. Next evidence action: attach one consolidated read-only evidence bundle and field-level rights matrix covering source provenance, permitted storage/caching/display/alerts, attribution, freshness, correction, takedown, alert identifiers and retention, deletion/access/correction, notification consent and unsubscribe behavior, GA4 settings, log fields, vendor/DPA coverage, and incident/request procedures. Keep outreach unsent and preserve the private gate.

Data-use dispositions: Woot API deal and price-history data is counsel_required and launch-blocked; user alert rules and sync results are evidence_needed; GA4 analytics is evidence_needed; operational logs and hosting data are evidence_needed. No item is clear. Ordinary fleet growth may continue only when existing consent, cookie/analytics disclosure, privacy and terms, affiliate disclosure, claims, provenance, copyright/trademark, platform-policy, and age-sensitive boundaries are preserved; incomplete telemetry alone is not a blocker.
